units.summary: The company identified freight document processing as its highest-priority use case.
units.quote: 3.1 Freight document processing (highest priority for the company)

units.summary: Mikko estimated approximately 1,200 freight documents per day across all sites; the estimate was to be checked against volume data.
units.quote: Mikko estimated about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. (To be checked against the volume data Jari will send - the TMS log may give a different number.)

units.summary: Mikko gave an alternative estimate of around 1,000 documents on a normal working day from the TMS log, noting that counting depends on when paper documents are scanned.
units.quote: I would say it's a bit less, maybe around 1,000 on a normal working day according to the TMS document log. But the log only counts paper documents when they are scanned, so it depends on how you count.

units.summary: Six document clerks manually enter freight document data into the TMS, with invoicing-relevant fields also entered in Business Central.
units.quote: Six document clerks (4 in Vantaa, 1 in Tampere, 1 in Oulu) key in the data manually into the TMS and, for invoicing-relevant fields, into Business Central.

units.summary: Mikko estimated that manual data entry has an error rate of around 4%; he also said finance spends about a day a week correcting errors.
units.quote: Mikko's estimate of the error rate in manual entry: around 4 %. Errors lead to wrong invoices, credit notes, and disputes; the finance team spends "a day a week" on corrections.

units.summary: The process map estimates 3–4 minutes per document for manual data entry, in addition to about one minute to find the shipment in the TMS.
units.quote:
~1 min

→

**7. Key in data**
Packages, weight, pallets, date, signature, remarks
3–4 min / doc ~4 % errors

units.summary: The company processed 71% of PODs within two days of delivery.
The invoice correction rate was 3.1%, against a target below 1%; the overview attributes it mainly to document entry errors.
units.quote:
Invoice correction rate
< 1 %
3.1 %
Mainly caused by document entry
errors

units.topic: document processing delay and claims risk
units.summary: Subcontractor documents may arrive 2–10 days late, and handwritten damage or shortage remarks are often noticed after the seven-day deadline for claiming against a haulier.
units.quote: Documents from subcontractors arrive with a delay of 2–10 days, and invoicing of a shipment cannot be completed until its POD has been processed. Remarks about damage or shortages written by hand on the documents are often noticed late, after the deadline for raising a claim against the haulier (7 days under the company's subcontracting terms).

units.summary: The desired concept is to extract fields into the TMS, require human review only for low-confidence documents, and flag handwritten remarks.
units.quote: Desired outcome: automatic extraction of the fields into the TMS with a human check only for low-confidence documents; flagging of handwritten remarks.

units.summary: The advisors identified handwriting as the main technical risk and said it should be tested using real documents.
units.quote: Handwriting is the main risk; must be tested on real samples.

units.summary: The advisors recommended beginning with one document type, POD, at one site, Vantaa, before scaling.
units.quote: Start with one document type (POD) and one site (Vantaa) before scaling.

units.summary: The requested pilot sample was 200 anonymised freight documents across types, sites, and languages, including at least 50 with handwritten remarks.
units.quote:
Jari: send anonymised sample of 200 freight documents (mix of types, sites, languages, at least
    50 with handwritten remarks) - by 30 October 2026.

units.summary: The TMS REST API supports single records only; bulk export is a paid service.
units.quote:
REST API (single records
only), WMS, driver
mobile app

units.summary: Overtime costs were EUR 410,000, and Tampere was identified as the worst-affected site due to irregular volumes from a large spare-parts customer.
units.quote:
Overtime and last-minute agency staff are costly. Mikko: overtime costs were about EUR 410,000 in
  2025, with the Tampere site the worst because of one large spare-parts customer with very
  irregular volumes.

units.summary: The proposed forecast would predict daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines for each warehouse one to three weeks ahead, using WMS history, customer forecasts, calendar effects, and possibly weather.
units.quote:
Idea: forecast daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines per warehouse 1-3 weeks ahead, using
  history from the WMS plus customer forecasts, calendar effects (holidays, campaigns), and maybe
  weather for the chilled food customers.

units.summary: The notes report six years of WMS history, but Jari was unsure whether pre-2020 data was comparable; Oulu data begins in 2023.
units.quote:
Six years of history exist in the WMS, but the system was replaced/upgraded in 2020 and Jari is not
  sure whether pre-2020 data is comparable. Oulu has only data since 2023.

units.summary: Only about a third of key customers regularly provide volume forecasts for staffing.
units.quote: Only about a third of the key customers send forecasts regularly.

units.summary: The advisors said forecasting depends on data quality and that a data extract should be assessed first.
units.quote: Forecasting is valuable but depends on data quality - need a data extract first.

units.summary: The shared customer service mailbox receives roughly 380 emails per day on average and more than 600 per day at the December peak.
units.quote:
Roughly 380 emails per day on
  average, peaking at over 600 in December.

units.summary: The customer service email response-time target is four hours; the 2025 average was 6.2 hours and the December average was 9.4 hours.
units.quote:
Customer service email response
time
4 h
6.2 h (avg), 9.4 h
(Dec)

units.summary: The proposed concept is to classify incoming emails, route them, retrieve shipment status from the TMS, and draft replies for an agent to approve; fully automatic replies were not desired at this stage.
units.quote:
Idea: automatically classify incoming emails, route them, look up shipment status from the TMS and
  draft a reply for the agent to approve. Not interested in fully automatic replies at this stage.

units.topic: customer service data and compliance constraint
units.summary: Customer service emails may contain consumer names, phone numbers, and home delivery addresses; GDPR and AI Act transparency questions were raised about access and data processing location.
units.quote:
Emails contain personal data (names, phone numbers, home delivery addresses of consumers for
  e-commerce customers). GDPR and AI Act transparency questions came up - who can see what, where the
  data is processed.

units.topic: customer service use case compliance effort
units.summary: The advisors considered email triage relatively easy technically but said it had the most compliance work and would be a good second step once an AI policy exists.
units.quote:
Email triage is relatively easy technically but has the most compliance work; good second step
  once an AI policy exists.

units.summary: The advisors identified the single-person IT function as a bottleneck and said any solution must be low-maintenance or operated by a partner.
units.quote: Risk: single IT person = bottleneck. Any solution must be low-maintenance or partner-operated.

units.summary: The company overview says the 2027 budget proposal earmarks EUR 50,000 for digitalisation and AI pilots, in addition to ordinary IT operating costs.
units.quote:
Budget: The 2027 budget proposal earmarks EUR 50,000 for digitalisation and AI pilots, in
addition to ordinary IT operating costs (approx. EUR 210,000 per year).

units.summary: Kaisa said the board would be open to investing EUR 60,000–80,000 in AI-related projects if the first pilot shows results.
units.quote:
Budget: Kaisa said the board would be open to investing EUR 60,000-80,000 in AI-related projects in
  2027 if the first pilot shows results.

units.summary: The strategy sets a goal to reduce manual work in office processes by 30%.
units.quote:
Operational excellence – reduce manual work in office processes by 30 % by the end of 2028
so that growth does not require additional office staff.

conflicts.description: The meeting notes estimate about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The recording gives an alternative estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day from the TMS log and notes that scanning practices affect the count. The instructions establish no source priority, so the estimates remain unresolved.

The company overview describes a 2027 budget proposal earmarking EUR 50,000 for digitalisation and AI pilots. The meeting notes report that the board would be open to investing EUR 60,000–80,000 in AI-related projects in 2027 if the first pilot shows results. The sources do not establish priority or reconcile the different figures, so the conflict is unresolved.
